## Rationale
The mathematical section of an early KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 draft is not yet a proof; several statements presented as 'derivations' are actually definitions or conditional constructions, and must be tightened before registration [S2821]. Uses a courtship-signal example (A signals B; B's response in {accept, ignore, reject, challenge, redirect}) to argue that a receiver's non-acceptance response constrains the admissible hypothesis space rather than delivering a definite truth value: Rejection != False and Silence != Zero, making biological communication a natural laboratory for studying negative information [S2821].

## All rows (source_id order)
- [S2821] types=[WARNING, ANALYSIS] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "The mathematical section of an early KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 draft is not yet a proof; several statements presented as 'derivations' are actually definitions or conditional constructions, and must be tightened before registration." (anchor: "Given the standards we have established for KnowledgeOS, I would tighten that before registering it.")
- [S2821] types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "The preservation-Zero criterion has two dual formulations that must not be identified prematurely: a quotient/equivalence formulation (K1 ~_Pi K2 iff indistinguishable under the preservation contract, giving Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff T(D) ~_Pi T(E_S(D))) and an observation/projection formulation (Pi:K->V a contract-relevant observation, giving Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D)))); an equivalence relation induces a quotient map but an arbitrary projection operator has additional algebraic properties that need not hold." (anchor: "Quotient/equivalence formulation ... Observation/projection formulation ... These can be related, but we shouldn't identify them prematurely.")
- [S2821] types=[CORRECTION, FORMALIZATION, HYPOTHESIS] scope=OBJECT — "The claimed derivation that cancellation-loop or non-linear-interaction cases prove emergent (in)dispensability is not a proof but a constructive witness; the rigorous reformulation is an existential witness search: does there exist f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} such that Zero(S)=f(Zero(s_1),...,Zero(s_n)) for every admissible sequence ('element-wise compositional'), tested by seeking two sequences with identical element-level Zero signatures z(S1)=z(S2) but Zero(S1)!=Zero(S2), which would show element-level Zero information is insufficient; connects to the prior finding that group Zero cannot generally be reconstructed from singleton Zero status." (anchor: "So the proper terminology is: Proposition candidate ... Element-level Zero does not determine sequence-level Zero.")
- [S2821] types=[CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "The claim that projection structure 'mathematically guarantees' contract relativity is weakened: it is only possible, not guaranteed, for two genuinely different observations Pi1,Pi2,Pi3 to disagree; the correct conditional statement is that if Pi3 retains a distinction discarded by Pi2, contract-relative Zero CAN differ, and this requires an actual witness Zero_{Pi2}(S)!=Zero_{Pi3}(S), not an automatic empirical fact." (anchor: "So the correct statement is: If Pi_3 retains a distinction discarded by Pi_2, then contract-relative Zero can differ.")
- [S2821] types=[DEFINITION, CORRECTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Determination(Q) should not be defined as entropy/cardinality reduction to one cause, since |H|=1 does not imply Truth and |H|>1 does not imply no actionable decision; instead Determination(Q) is redefined as a contract-defined admissibility condition over the hypothesis space H_Q." (anchor: "Determination(Q) = contract-defined admissibility condition over H_Q.")
- [S2821] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Actionable closure is defined as policy invariance rather than epistemic uniqueness: for an action set A and policy pi:H_Q->A, ActionStable(H_Q) iff |pi(H_Q)|=1, meaning all currently admissible hypotheses lead to the same action; |H_Q|>1 can coexist with |pi(H_Q)|=1, so 'actionable closure does not require epistemic uniqueness.'" (anchor: "ActionStable(H_Q) iff |pi(H_Q)| = 1. ... Actionable closure does not require epistemic uniqueness.")
- [S2821] types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Proposes an 8-stage epistemic pipeline (Signal->Observation->Evidence->Hypothesis Space->Assessment->Determination->Decision->Action) with Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) operating orthogonally to it rather than as another stage in the pipeline, giving the non-equivalence chain Zero != Rejection != Silence != Determination != Decision." (anchor: "Signal -> Observation -> Evidence -> Hypothesis Space -> Assessment -> Determination -> Decision -> Action ... Zero != Rejection != Silence != Determination != Decision.")
- [S2821] types=[GOVERNANCE, RESTATEMENT] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Recommends re-tagging each of the draft's claimed 'derivations' by honest epistemic status (formal definition; existential research hypothesis/witness search x2; conditional formal proposition; candidate formal definition; [EXT][RESEARCH LENS]; [OPEN][PROP]) and retitling the document 'KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 -- Formal Foundations and Testable Propositions' rather than 'mathematical derivation.'" (anchor: "| Section | Correct status | ... So I would not call the document "mathematical derivation" yet.")
- [S2821] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXTENSION] scope=OBJECT — "Adopts an ordered interaction-trace carrier C^{t:n}=[(M_1,R_1,t_1),...,(M_n,R_n,t_n)] enabling independent investigation of elements, pairs, composed pairs, subsequences, and full traces, raising whether time/order itself is epistemically relevant; recommends adding a fourth object 'Interaction History' Hist(C^{t:n}) alongside Element/Relation/Sequence since provenance may be non-reducible, with terminal equivalence, epistemic equivalence, and historical equivalence not required to coincide (K1=K2 does not imply Hist1=Hist2)." (anchor: "Using C^{t:n}=[(M_1,R_1,t_1),...,(M_n,R_n,t_n)] gives us a genuine ordered carrier.")
- [S2821] types=[DISTINCTION, WARNING] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Observed order sensitivity (Zero(T(C1 o C2)) != Zero(T(C2 o C1)) for a tested system) is weaker than proving algebraic non-commutativity (C1 o C2 != C2 o C1), which requires a defined algebraic carrier and equality; the correct progression is observed order sensitivity -> candidate algebraic non-commutativity -> formal algebraic test." (anchor: "observed order sensitivity -> candidate algebraic non-commutativity -> formal algebraic test.")
- [S2821] types=[ARGUMENT, DISTINCTION, EXAMPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Uses a courtship-signal example (A signals B; B's response in {accept, ignore, reject, challenge, redirect}) to argue that a receiver's non-acceptance response constrains the admissible hypothesis space rather than delivering a definite truth value: Rejection != False and Silence != Zero, making biological communication a natural laboratory for studying negative information." (anchor: "Rejection != False and Silence != Zero.")
- [S2821] types=[PRINCIPLE, GOVERNANCE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Proposes a cross-lens table (Vedic, information theory, Bayesian, Kalman/control, logic, knowledge graph, cybernetics, biological communication), reframing the research question as whether independent lenses repeatedly expose the same structural capability (strengthening candidacy for formal investigation) rather than assuming they describe the same thing; explicitly decides NOT to execute the biological experiment yet, deferring to formalizing a witness generator for five witness types W1-W5 across synthetic traces and the existing Zero-algebra environment before any structural-principle claim." (anchor: "Do independent lenses repeatedly expose the same structural capability? ... Convergence of metaphors != proof of kernel necessity.")
- [S2822] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Specifies five formal witness generators for KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01: W1 tests z(C1)=z(C2) with Zero(C1)!=Zero(C2) (non-elementarity); W2 tests Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) (order sensitivity, not intrinsic non-commutativity); W3 tests whether S shifts from eliminable to indispensable purely as a function of preservation scope, proving Zero is a relational property of (S,D,T,Pi,Q,C); W4 tests |pi(H_Q)|=1 while |H_Q|>1 (decision resolution decoupled from epistemic resolution); W5 tests K1=K2 with Hist1!=Hist2 (historical provenance non-reducible to current state)." (anchor: "W_1: Non-Elementarity Witness Generator (Signature Insufficiency) ... W_5: History / Terminal-State Divergence Witness Generator")
- [S2822] types=[CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "W1's witness must explicitly hold the same T,Pi,Q,C and admissibility conditions constant across C1,C2, otherwise the non-elementarity result could be an artifact of a changed contract or context rather than genuine signature insufficiency." (anchor: "W1 needs one more condition ... Otherwise the result could simply be caused by changing the contract or context.")
- [S2822] types=[CORRECTION, DISTINCTION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "W4 (decision stability without epistemic uniqueness) should be tagged [PROP][OPEN] Decision/Epistemic Resolution rather than being allowed to become evidence for Zero itself, since it belongs to the Determination->Decision boundary rather than Zero algebra." (anchor: "W4 is mathematically clean, but it is not really a Zero experiment ... it belongs primarily to the Determination -> Decision boundary, not to Zero algebra.")
- [S2822] types=[CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "W5's historical-divergence condition Hist(C1)!=Hist(C2) is corrected to non-equivalence under a declared provenance contract, Hist(C1) not-equiv_{Pi_prov} Hist(C2), since two representations could otherwise differ syntactically while being semantically identical." (anchor: "I would change Hist_1 != Hist_2 to non-equivalence under a declared provenance contract ... Hist(C_1) not equiv_{Pi_prov} Hist(C_2).")
- [S2822] types=[GOVERNANCE, PRINCIPLE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Rejects the protocol wording that cross-lens agreement is itself a promotion criterion; a candidate must still pass the existing chain Semantic Contract -> Capability -> Simulation -> Irreducibility -> Minimality, preserving the established rule that convergence of metaphors is not proof of kernel necessity." (anchor: "Cross-lens agreement = corroborating evidence, not proof of kernel membership. ... Semantic Contract -> Capability -> Simulation -> Irreducibility -> Minimality.")
- [S2822] types=[DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Identifies two distinct research layers within the KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 programme: Layer A (Knowledge Algebra) investigating Element->Relation->Sequence->History and whether Zero is element-wise compositional, order-dependent, or scope-dependent; Layer B (Knowledge Theory) investigating Evidence->Hypotheses->Determination->Decision and whether action can stabilize without causal determination." (anchor: "Layer A -- Knowledge Algebra ... Layer B -- Knowledge Theory")
